title: Time-to-live allocations: never refresh data that dies first
idea: Time shift from the fixed 64 ms refresh clock to software data lifetimes: allocators (malloc, PyTorch caching allocator, NIC buffers) tag buffers with a TTL, and the memory controller keeps a per-row 'expires-at' timestamp, skipping refresh for rows whose contents will be overwritten or freed before their retention bin runs out and stopping refresh on freed rows entirely.
why: Refresh energy/bandwidth (fact 3): in AI training/inference 50-80% of DRAM bytes are short-lived tensors living <30 ms, so refresh operations drop ~2-4x and refresh's share of idle power falls from ~25% to <10%.

title: Fleet-learned per-row retention atlas built over years
idea: Scale jump from one DIMM to a million-server fleet and time jump from a 64 ms spec to multi-year observation: every server runs low-priority retention probes (write pattern, pause 0.25-4 s, read) in idle banks and uploads per-row results with temperature; a fleet model keyed by die lot, wafer position and age assigns each row a refresh bin loaded at boot, and repeated sightings flag variable-retention cells.
why: Refresh (fact 3): >99.9% of rows retain >1 s, so binning most rows to 256 ms-1 s cuts refresh ops ~4-8x, while fleet statistics catch rare VRT behaviour that a single factory test cannot see.

title: 77 K co-designed DRAM pool with refresh switched off
idea: Scale jump from device to rack plus a time jump in retention: a CXL memory rack immersed in liquid nitrogen with DRAM redesigned for 77 K, with access-transistor Vt lowered ~0.3 V (subthreshold slope ~20 mV/dec at 77 K), VARY dropped to ~0.6 V and wordline to ~1.8 V, so leakage collapses by >10 decades and refresh is replaced by an hourly scrub.
why: Eliminates refresh energy and bandwidth (fact 3) and breaks the voltage floor (fact 10): ~3-5x lower CV^2 array energy, with cryocooler overhead amortized across a rack-scale shared pool.

title: Global pulse self-restore: whole-die refresh in one nanosecond broadcast
idea: Time shift from serial row-by-row refresh (8k REF commands per 64 ms) to one die-wide pulse: each cell adds a tiny gain transistor gated by its own storage node, with its drain on a shared 'restore' mesh; pulsing the mesh to VARY for ~2 ns tops up every node still reading '1' (gain device on) and leaves '0' nodes untouched, with no wordline, bitline or sense-amp activity.
why: Refresh bandwidth loss (10-20%, fact 3) goes to ~0 and refresh energy falls ~20-50x because only cell charge moves, not bitlines; the 2T cell costs ~40% area, offset if it relaxes capacitor targets (fact 1).

title: Deuterium-hardened access stack starves variable-retention traps
idea: Scale jump down to the atomic nucleus: replace hydrogen with deuterium in the final forming-gas anneal and in SiN/SiO2 precursors around the access transistor and storage junction; the heavier Si-D bond resists breaking, so fewer interface and junction traps form over life and fewer metastable defects toggle, which is the source of variable retention time.
why: Leakage tail (fact 3): VRT and trap-assisted GIDL dominate the <=13 fA tail; the isotope effect cuts hot-carrier trap generation 10-50x in logic, so a 2-4x tighter retention tail and longer refresh interval are plausible.

title: Wordline Joule self-annealing heals the retention tail yearly
idea: Time shift from a one-time fab anneal to in-field anneals every year, and scale shift to a single row: in maintenance windows the controller drives DC current along selected buried wordlines (small potential difference between both ends) to heat the access region locally to ~250-300 C for milliseconds, annealing the metastable defects behind VRT cells found by retention profiling.
why: Leakage tail/refresh (fact 3) and lifetime drift: removing the worst ~0.01% of cells lets the refresh-bin floor rise ~2x and reverses aging-induced tail growth.

title: Majority-value bitline parking during long idle
idea: Time shift from ns-scale active behaviour to seconds-long standby: when a subarray idles >1 ms, a per-subarray ones-counter (updated on writes) decides whether most cells hold '1' or '0' and bitlines are parked at VARY or ground instead of VARY/2, so the majority of cells see ~0 V drain-source and stop subthreshold leaking; minority cells get a shorter refresh bin.
why: Idle refresh energy (fact 3, 16-33% of idle power): data skew (zeros dominate sparse ML tensors) lets 70-90% of cells stop channel leakage, extending effective standby retention ~2-3x.

title: Access-scheduled refresh: OS rotates hot pages across every row
idea: Scale jump from DRAM rows to OS page tables and time shift to workload access intervals: the kernel and a controller indirection table periodically re-place frequently touched pages so natural activations sweep every physical row within its retention window, and rows activated recently are logged and skipped by refresh.
why: Refresh ops/bandwidth (fact 3): in bandwidth-heavy AI serving, explicit refresh is cut 40-70%; spreading activations also lowers per-row hammer counts (fact 9).

title: Let cells decay: soft-decision LDPC reads stretched-refresh charge
idea: Time shift: deliberately run refresh at 1-2 s and treat retention loss as a noisy channel; sense amplifiers add a second offset reference so each read also returns a 'weak' flag, and an on-die LDPC decoder uses those soft bits to correct 1e-4-class decay errors, scrubbing rows whose weak-flag count rises.
why: Refresh energy/bandwidth (fact 3): 16-32x fewer refreshes for ~6-10% parity overhead, importing NAND's soft-decision playbook into DRAM timescales.

title: Room-temperature Coulomb-blockade island isolates the storage node
idea: Scale jump to the few-nanometre quantum dot: insert a sub-2 nm silicon nanocrystal between access channel and storage node so the single-electron charging energy (~200-300 meV) exceeds 8 kT; in hold the bias sits inside the blockade window so leakage is exponentially suppressed, while the wordline shifts the dot level to allow ns sequential tunnelling during access.
why: Access leakage tail (fact 3): blockade adds 4-6 decades of off-state suppression independent of transistor Vt, potentially minutes of retention.

title: Refresh-interval SKUs: sell DRAM priced by retention bin
idea: Scale jump from wafer sort to market structure: test every die at four refresh intervals (64 ms, 256 ms, 1 s, 4 s at 85 C) and sell long-retention grades at a premium to phones, IoT and cold CXL tiers running relaxed refresh, while short-retention dies go to always-busy AI servers whose traffic refreshes rows anyway.
why: Usable supply and yield (strategy): dies now derated or scrapped for tail retention become sellable, and long-retention bins cut device idle power 15-30%.

title: Canary-cell event-driven refresh replaces the fixed clock
idea: Time shift from clock-driven (fixed 64 ms) to event-driven refresh: each subarray carries a row of deliberately weakened canary cells (smaller capacitor, slightly lower Vt) whose leakage tracks 2x the true array tail; a comparator watches them and the bank refreshes only when a canary crosses threshold, automatically tracking temperature, voltage and aging.
why: Refresh energy (fact 3): removes the 4-8x worst-case guardband baked into fixed intervals; at 45 C refresh ops fall ~4x.

title: Idle rows nap in a charge-trap shadow inside the access gate
idea: Two timescales in one cell: the access transistor gate stack gets a thin SiN charge-trap layer; when a row has idled >1 s the controller applies one program pulse that copies each bit (via the storage-node-dependent channel potential) into trapped charge and stops refreshing the row; on the next access a Vt-shift sense restores the DRAM charge, so trap endurance is spent only on idle transitions (~1e6 over life).
why: Idle refresh power (16-33% of idle, fact 3) goes to ~0 for cold data, the majority of server capacity, while hot rows keep ns DRAM access.

title: Resonant LC wordline drivers recycle refresh energy
idea: Time shift that exploits refresh's metronome-like periodicity: because refresh activations arrive on a fixed cadence, refresh wordlines and sense-amp enables are driven from an on-package LC tank tuned to that cadence, swinging the ~3 V wordline adiabatically and returning ~60-70% of the CV^2 charge to the tank instead of dumping it from a charge pump.
why: Refresh energy and voltage floor (facts 3, 10): wordline boost pumps are ~30-40% efficient, so adiabatic driving cuts refresh wordline energy ~3x, borrowing resonant clocking from CPUs.

title: Tail rows exiled to an on-die SRAM jail
idea: Scale shift: the ppm-scale retention tail is served by a tiny memory with a different timescale; rows or 64 B segments failing a 1 s retention test at sort or in the field are remapped through a CAM into a few hundred KB of on-die SRAM or fast-refresh eDRAM, letting the rest of the array run at 1 s refresh.
why: Refresh (fact 3): ~16x fewer refresh ops for <0.5% die area, because the long tail sits in ~1e-5 of rows.

title: Two gates in series on one pillar: stack-effect leakage suppression
idea: Scale jump that folds logic's standby 'transistor stacking' trick into one vertical-channel access pillar with two independently driven gate segments (upper and lower wordline); both turn on for access, but in hold the intermediate node floats up a few hundred mV, putting the upper device at negative VGS with reduced DIBL.
why: Subthreshold leakage tail (fact 3): the stack effect cuts off-current 10-30x, enabling 4F^2 vertical cells with ~1 s retention.

title: Light-gated access: optical wordlines and dark-off photoconductive switches
idea: Scale jump from fibre optics to the cell: replace the electrically gated access transistor with a wide-bandgap photoconductive bridge (e.g., SiC or diamond-like carbon film) addressed by on-chip waveguide wordlines; in the dark the bridge is an insulator with no thermal carriers across ~3 eV, and a ~100 ps blue/UV pulse along the waveguide row makes it conduct for read or write.
why: Leakage/refresh (fact 3) and the 3 V wordline (fact 10): no gate voltage at all and dark leakage set by bandgap, potentially seconds-to-hours retention.

title: JEDEC refresh-hint command lets software own retention time
idea: Scale shift from silicon to standards: define a REFHINT/RETAIN command for DDR6, LPDDR6 and CXL.mem carrying per-range 'live until' and 'tolerates N errors' fields that DRAM self-refresh logic honours, plus a vendor-published per-bank retention-curve register.
why: Refresh energy and bandwidth (fact 3): makes software TTL and approximate regions portable across vendors, turning 2-5x refresh reductions into an ecosystem default.

title: Bit-plane split: mantissa low bits live in relaxed-refresh banks
idea: Scale shift down to the bits inside a number: the controller transposes FP16/BF16 tensors so sign, exponent and top mantissa bits sit in normally refreshed banks while low mantissa bits sit in banks refreshed every 2-4 s, where occasional decay only perturbs the 4th-7th significant bit.
why: Refresh energy (fact 3): ~40-50% of weight/activation bits get 30-60x fewer refreshes with <0.1% accuracy impact in tolerant layers.

title: Dual-timescale back-gate: deep negative bias only during idle seconds
idea: Time shift between access bursts (ns) and idle stretches (s): build the array on thin-BOX SOI with a per-bank back-gate plane held near 0 V during bursts for strong on-current, then pumped to about -2 V after ~10 us idle, raising access-transistor Vt ~200-300 mV and cutting subthreshold leakage ~100x.
why: Idle refresh power (fact 3): self-refresh interval stretches 10-50x in idle-dominated mobile and server profiles with no access-speed penalty.

title: Compress years of VRT behaviour into minutes at wafer sort
idea: Time shift: accelerate rare variable-retention-time toggling (dwell times of hours at 85 C) with a sort step combining 150 C, cyclic bias-temperature stress on wordlines and a hydrogen-rich ambient, so metastable traps toggle many times within minutes; cells seen toggling are fused out or binned.
why: Refresh guardband (fact 3): VRT is why vendors keep 64 ms though most cells hold seconds; catching VRT cells at test lets field refresh relax 4-8x.

title: Graded work-function wordline flattens the GIDL hotspot
idea: Scale shift into a nanometre composition profile: deposit the buried wordline as a laterally graded TiN-to-TiAlN stack (composition changing over ~10-20 nm) so the gate work function is lower facing the storage node and higher at the channel centre, reducing the gate-to-drain field that drives band-to-band tunnelling while keeping Vt high.
why: GIDL tail (fact 3): ~20-30% lower peak field gives ~10x lower GIDL and permits a smaller negative wordline bias (fact 10).

title: Rack-level erasure coding lets DIMMs refresh ten times slower
idea: Scale jump from on-die ECC to cross-server parity: a CXL memory pool stripes each cache line plus parity across 10+2 memory nodes, each node refreshes only every ~0.5-1 s, and any decayed row is reconstructed from the other nodes and rewritten, so the rack, not the cell, guarantees retention.
why: Refresh energy at datacenter scale (fact 3): 8-16x fewer refreshes for ~20% parity overhead, plus reuse of retention-weak dies otherwise scrapped.

title: Heteroepitaxial 3C-SiC access pillar: retention from milliseconds to hours
idea: Time shift through bandgap: grow the vertical access-channel pillars as 3C-SiC (Si and C only, N/Al dopants) on the Si wafer; SiC's intrinsic carrier density (~1e-1 cm^-3 versus 1e10 for Si) suppresses generation and band-to-band leakage by >10 decades, so retention becomes limited by the capacitor dielectric instead of the transistor.
why: Leakage tail/refresh (fact 3): minutes-to-hours retention removes >99% of refresh; all elements Earth-abundant, no W or Hf in the device.

title: Atomic aluminate dipole sets threshold, channel left undoped
idea: Scale shift from statistical dopant atoms (~10-20 randomly placed per channel at F=12 nm) to one deterministic atomic sheet: a ~0.3 nm AlOx layer at the gate-dielectric/SiO2 interface forms a dipole shifting nFET Vt by +0.2-0.4 V, so the access channel can be left undoped; lower doping lowers the storage-junction field and collapses the trap-assisted tunnelling and GIDL that form the tail.
why: Leakage tail (fact 3): random dopant fluctuation and high junction fields cause the <=13 fA tail; expect a 3-10x tighter tail using only Al and O.

title: Solar-cell field-effect passivation transplanted onto storage-node sidewalls
idea: Scale jump from square-metre solar cells to 15 nm cell pillars: line the isolation sidewalls where the storage junction's depletion region meets the surface with ALD Al2O3 carrying ~-5e12 cm^-2 fixed charge (the PERC passivation trick), keeping the p-well surface accumulated so surface SRH generation, a major junction-leakage source, shuts off.
why: Junction leakage/refresh (fact 3): solar passivation lowers surface recombination ~100x; at DRAM pitch where surface-to-volume is huge, expect 2-5x lower junction leakage with Al and O only.

title: Silicon NEMS relay as access switch: an air gap never leaks
idea: Scale jump from the telephone relay to a 60 nm silicon beam: each cell's access device is a doubly clamped Si beam pulled onto a TiN contact by the wordline's electrostatic force; when released, a ~5 nm gap gives effectively zero off-current, so retention is limited only by the capacitor dielectric.
why: Leakage/refresh (fact 3): channel leakage vanishes and refresh intervals stretch to seconds-minutes; switching ~1-5 ns at this scale; the risk is stiction and >1e15-cycle contact endurance; materials Si, Ti, N only.

title: Nano-vacuum field-emission access: a vacuum tube shrunk to 10 nm
idea: Scale jump from 1940s vacuum tubes to a sealed ~10 nm cavity: a sharpened Si tip on the storage-node side faces a Si/TiN collector across vacuum, encircled by a gate ring; Fowler-Nordheim emission turns on exponentially only above a gate-field threshold, and below it the gap holds no carriers at all.
why: Access leakage (fact 3) set by tunnelling through vacuum (vanishingly small), so retention is bounded by the dielectric; Si/O/Ti/N only; speculative on emission uniformity and ns-scale current.

title: Charge-plasma junctions: abundant-metal work functions replace implanted dopants
idea: Scale shift from implanted dopant atoms to an electric field: the access transistor's source/drain are induced electrostatically by low-work-function Mg- or Al-capped contacts (~3.7-4.1 eV) beside an undoped Si channel gated by a NiSi/TiN gate, so no metallurgical p-n junction sits at the storage node, which is the main seat of junction and trap-assisted leakage.
why: Junction leakage tail (fact 3): removes implant damage and dopant-related traps, ~5-10x lower junction leakage; no Hf, W or Co.

title: Copper buried wordline with self-forming manganese silicate barrier
idea: Scale shift of a BEOL interconnect trick (um) into the ~10 nm buried-wordline trench, plus a time shift in row cycle: fill with CuMn alloy and anneal so Mn diffuses to the SiO2 liner and forms a ~1 nm self-aligned MnSiOx barrier, replacing TiN/W fill and avoiding TaN; the lower RC shortens every refresh row activation.
why: W chokepoint (China ~80%) plus refresh time (fact 3): ~3x lower wordline resistance trims tRFC/row cycle ~20-30%, recovering refresh bandwidth; risk is Cu diffusion into the channel.

title: Millisecond flash anneal grows rutile TiO2 capacitor without ruthenium
idea: Time shift in processing: replace the Ru/RuO2 template normally needed for high-k rutile TiO2 with a ~1 ms flash-lamp or laser anneal that drives as-deposited Al-doped TiO2 on TiN through the anatase-to-rutile transition before the TiN oxidizes, yielding k~80-100.
why: Capacitor charge wall (fact 1) feeding retention (fact 3): ~2x Cs at the same aspect ratio doubles retention (halves refresh) or lets AR drop ~2x; removes Ru and Hf dependence.

title: ZnON back-end access tier stacked over the periphery
idea: Scale shift from front-end silicon to the back end of line: build access transistors in zinc oxynitride (Zn, O, N; no In or Ga) at <=400 C directly above the CMOS sense amplifiers and stack 4-8 tiers; the wide bandgap and absence of hole conduction give ~1e-18 A/um off-current while ~50-100 cm^2/Vs mobility keeps ns access.
why: Periphery area (fact 7, 49% of die) is reclaimed by building the array over it, and leakage (fact 3) falls so refresh stretches to seconds, without IGZO's In/Ga chokepoints.

title: Silicon-on-nothing: each storage junction floats over a sealed void
idea: Scale shift from MEMS cavities to the single cell: use the silicon-only empty-space-in-silicon process (trench array plus high-temperature H2 anneal so Si surface-migrates into a sealed buried void) to put a vacuum void directly under each storage-node junction, removing bottom junction area and blocking substrate minority-carrier diffusion.
why: Junction leakage (fact 3): bottom-area and diffusion terms are often >50% of junction leakage, so ~2-4x retention gain with only Si and H2.

title: Carbon co-implant gettering scrubs iron from storage junctions
idea: Scale shift to ppb impurities: a single mid-gap Fe or Ni atom in a depletion region can create a 1e-9 tail cell, so carbon is implanted a few hundred nm below the array (with an oxygen-precipitate denuded zone) and C-related complexes getter transition metals away from storage junctions throughout the thermal budget.
why: Leakage tail (fact 3): tail cells are often single-defect; gettering targets 2-5x fewer tail cells and longer refresh bins using only carbon.

title: Epitaxial CaF2 gate insulator: a crystal, not a glass
idea: Scale shift from amorphous oxide to an atom-by-atom lattice: grow single-crystal CaF2 (lattice-matched to Si within ~0.6%) as the access-transistor gate dielectric so the interface is nearly trap-free and gate tunnelling at ~1 nm EOT is lower than SiO2; fewer interface traps means fewer trap-assisted GIDL and VRT sites.
why: Leakage tail/VRT (fact 3) and voltage floor (fact 10, thinner EOT allows lower wordline voltage); Ca and F are abundant; risk is CaF2 epitaxy on 3D pillar sidewalls.

title: Microsecond laser seeded recrystallization makes single-grain stacked access transistors
idea: Time shift in thermal processing: deposit amorphous Si for each 3D-DRAM tier, then sweep a microsecond-pulse laser so melt fronts grow laterally from a seed opening, giving one grain per access transistor while the short melt keeps lower tiers below 450 C.
why: No manufacturable 3D cell (fact 2): grain-boundary-free silicon gives bulk-like low leakage for lateral access transistors across 26+ tiers using only Si, with no IGZO In/Ga.

title: Porous-silicon sacrificial tiers replace SiGe in 3D DRAM stacks
idea: Scale shift from bulk electrochemistry (porous Si for MEMS and solar) to 3D-DRAM tier formation: grow alternating heavily boron-doped and lightly doped Si epilayers, anodize only the heavy layers into porous Si through slit trenches, then oxidize or etch them away to release lateral access-transistor layers, avoiding scarce Ge and SiGe misfit defects.
why: 3D cell blocker (fact 2): strain-free, defect-free lateral channels shrink the leakage tail and simplify 30+ tier stacks using Si, B and HF chemistry only.

title: Airgap between buried wordlines kills passing-gate leakage
idea: Scale shift from BEOL low-k airgaps down to the buried-wordline level: after wordline recess, ash out a sacrificial carbon liner between adjacent wordline trenches to leave sealed airgaps (k=1), so an active neighbour wordline no longer capacitively lifts the access channel or injects carriers into adjacent storage nodes.
why: Passing-gate leakage and hammer-induced charge loss (facts 3, 9): ~2-3x lower coupling means fewer prematurely decaying cells and less refresh and mitigation overhead, using C and O2 only.

title: Refresh locked to the rhythm of AI training steps
idea: Time shift by synchronizing two clocks: AI accelerators run near-periodic steps (forward, backward, all-reduce) with predictable memory-idle phases; the runtime publishes a phase schedule and the memory controller bunches refresh bursts into compute-bound and all-reduce windows on plain silicon DRAM with no new elements.
why: Refresh bandwidth loss (10-20%, fact 3) is >90% hidden with zero material change; the constraint pushes the gain into timing instead of chemistry.

title: HBM stack thermal gradient: long-lived data sinks to cooler dies
idea: Scale shift to the stack: HBM layers run at different temperatures (top dies 5-15 C hotter), so the controller sets a per-die refresh interval from on-die sensors and migrates long-lived, rarely accessed pages to the coolest layers while frequently touched (naturally refreshed) data lives in the hottest ones.
why: Refresh energy (fact 3): retention halves per ~10 C, so per-die binning and placement cut refresh ~30-50% in unmodified Si/Cu HBM.

title: Slow-tier thick-oxide cell trades 30 ns for ten-second retention
idea: Time trade inside the access device: a capacity-tier DRAM built with 5-6 nm SiO2, long-channel, high-Vt access transistors at relaxed pitch accepts tRCD ~30-40 ns in exchange for ~10 s retention, with wide parallel interfaces hiding latency for bulk AI weights.
why: Refresh (fact 3) nearly eliminated, and capital (fact 4): the tier can run on depreciated 28-40 nm DUV fabs in the U.S. using only Si, SiO2, TiN, Al and Cu.

title: Biased deep carrier-sink layer shields arrays from substrate leakage
idea: Scale shift of the analog guard ring (100 um) to every array mat: implant a deep, positively biased phosphorus collector layer under each mat inside a boron array well so thermally generated substrate electrons are collected before they diffuse into storage nodes.
why: Diffusion component of junction leakage (fact 3), dominant at 85 C: ~2-5x retention at high temperature using only B and P implants.

title: Image-sensor pinned-photodiode storage: hold the bit like a dark pixel
idea: Scale and time shift from CMOS image sensors, whose pinned photodiodes hold charge 10-100 ms at ~1 e-/s dark current: store each bit as a charge packet in a fully depleted buried n-well capped by a p+ pinning layer, moved by a transfer gate onto a floating-diffusion gain node for sensing, so the pinned surface removes the interface generation that dominates DRAM leakage.
why: Leakage (fact 3): ~1 e-/s versus the DRAM tail of ~8e4 e-/s means minutes of retention with only ~1-2k electrons stored, also relaxing the capacitor charge wall (fact 1); Si, B, P only.

title: Silicon charge racetrack: CCD loops that refresh by moving
idea: Time shift: rather than holding charge still and refreshing it, data circulates as charge packets in short buried-channel CCD loops (e.g., 16 bits per vertical pillar) clocked at ~1-2 GHz with a regenerative re-inject stage per loop, so every bit is restored each ~10 ns loop and random access waits <=8 ns on average; silicon replaces magnetic racetrack's Co/Pt.
why: Refresh disappears as a separate operation and density rises (~16 bits per footprint, an alternative route around fact 2); Si/O/TiN only; risks are charge-transfer inefficiency and clock power.

title: Silicon feedback-FET access switch borrows thyristor latch physics
idea: Scale jump from kilovolt power thyristors to a 15 nm vertical gated p-i-n: charge held in spacer-adjacent potential barriers creates positive feedback so the device turns on at <5 mV/decade, letting a 1 V wordline swing span ~10 decades between on and off current instead of ~6-7.
why: Leakage tail and voltage floor (facts 3, 10): deeper off-state for the same swing, wordline voltage from ~3 V to ~1.5 V, using Si, B, P and SiO2 only.

title: Factory-injected nitride charge trims Vt of only the leakiest cells
idea: Time shift from ns operation to decade-long stored charge: the access transistor's spacer liner includes a SiN trap layer, and at wafer test cells found in the leakage tail receive a one-time high-field injection via their wordline/bitline that permanently stores electrons, raising their Vt ~150-250 mV for the product's 10-year life.
why: Leakage tail (fact 3): flattening the worst ~0.1% of cells lets the refresh interval rise 4-8x using only Si and N; risk is trapped-charge loss at 85 C over 10 years.
